title: Vibration Isolated Mounting for the Engine Electronic Control Unit
abstract: A proposed elastomeric mounting for the engine electronic control unit, launched against a vibration-driven connector wear finding and cancelled when the engine manufacturer solved the same problem inside the unit.

sections.reason: Shop reports on twenty-three engine electronic control units showed fretting on the airframe connector contacts, with the wear pattern matching the fan-speed vibration signature rather than any handling damage. The finding was concentrated on aircraft that had accumulated more than 12 000 flight cycles. At launch the airframe mounting was judged to be the shortest route to a fix, because it needed no change to the unit itself and could be embodied at an engine change.
sections.description: The proposal replaced the rigid mounting bracket D7320119707133 with an elastomeric isolator set tuned below the fan blade passing frequency, retained the unit seal D7320114580320 with a longer skirt to accommodate the additional movement, and protected the harness break-out with sleeving AES911172K8 where the relative motion is greatest. The unit firewall panel 1EF and the mount link 5EF8 would have kept their positions. Detail was carried on drawing D73201204106. Installation would have been done with the fan cowl doors open in zones 411, 421 and 452.
sections.effects: The proposal carried an estimated mass increase of 1.1 kg per engine and no electrical load change. It would not have been interchangeable with the rigid mounting because the bracket footprint changes. Design review raised a concern about isolator ageing in the nacelle thermal environment, which would have introduced a life limited part into an otherwise on-condition installation.
sections.embodiment_note: Cancelled in June 2024 before any aircraft was modified. The engine manufacturer introduced a revised connector retention inside the control unit under its own change process, which removed the fretting mechanism at source and made the airframe mounting change unnecessary. No production cut-in and no Service Bulletin were issued.
